title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology
abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

title: Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty. RESULTS: We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk. CONCLUSIONS: Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

title: Calcium Density as a Marker of Coronary Plaque Stabilization in Primary Prevention: The CAUGHT-CAD Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite primary prevention statin treatment, a substantial proportion of individuals remain at residual risk for cardiovascular events. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CTA) enables the quantification of compositional changes in calcified plaque. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine whether increases in coronary calcified plaque volume and density associated with statin therapy could be used as a marker of plaque stabilization in asymptomatic individuals undergoing serial coronary CTA. METHODS: In the CAUGHT-CAD trial, asymptomatic, statin-naive, intermediate-risk individuals were randomized to a primary prevention strategy (including statin treatment) vs usual care. Participants underwent coronary CTA at baseline and 3 years. In this post hoc analysis, volumes of 5 plaque subtypes were quantified: noncalcified (≤350 HU), low-density calcium (351-500 HU), intermediate-density calcium (501-700 HU), high-density calcium (701-1000 HU), and very high density calcium (>1,000 HU). The primary outcome was the per-lesion level change in volumes of calcified plaque subtypes. RESULTS: Eight hundred forty lesions were included from 338 participants (mean age: 58.3 ± 6.9 years, 57.1% men, 161 [47.6%] statin treated). Statin treatment was associated with greater progression in intermediate-density (β = 0.89, SE = 0.39; P = 0.02) and high-density (β = 0.79, SE = 0.24; P = 0.001) calcium, alongside regression of noncalcified plaque (β = -9.83, SE = 1.64; P < 0.001), following adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level, and baseline plaque volume. Among statin-treated participants, LDL-C reduction ≥30% was associated with greater progression of high-density (β = 1.11, SE = 0.49; P = 0.03) and very high density (β = 1.68, SE = 0.85; P = 0.04) calcium. CONCLUSIONS: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C. (Coronary Artery Calcium Score: Use to Guide Management of Hereditary Coronary Artery Disease [CAUGHT-CAD]; ACTRN12614001294640).

title: Global Prevalence of Adherence to Antihypertensives and Associated Moderating Factors Among Adults With Hypertension: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a significant public health issue affecting over a billion adults worldwide with adherence to antihypertensives being crucial for achieving sustained blood pressure control and reducing cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. To extend previous evidence, we conducted a meta-analysis on global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives among adults. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL. Pooled prevalence of antihypertensive medication adherence was estimated using generalized linear mixed-effects model in R software version 4.4.3. Cochran's Q, τ2, and I2$$ {I}^2 $$ statistics examined statistical heterogeneity with moderator analysis exploring sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis was analyzed using exact fixed-effects model. RESULTS: A total of 123 studies with 1 052 445 adults with hypertension were included. Pooled global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives was estimated at 58% (95% CI, 52%-63%), with 39% for high adherence, 29% for moderate adherence, and 35% for low adherence. Results for sensitivity analysis were 57.91% (95% CI, 57.81%-58.01%) with δ̂ being 24.3%. Prevalence across continents was 67% for Europe, 65% for South America, 60% for Africa, 56% for Asia, and 45% for North America. Adherence to antihypertensives was similar across low-income countries (61%), high-income countries (58), upper-middle-income countries (57%), and lower-middle-income countries (56%). In multivariate model, age and assessment tool only were significantly associated with medication adherence. CONCLUSIONS: Globally, a large proportion of adults with hypertension exhibit moderate to low adherence to antihypertensive medications. Future studies should prioritize establishing consensus-based operational definitions and cutoff values to enhance adherence.

title: Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT)
abstract: AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo. METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers. RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

title: Outcomes in patients with diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and heart failure treated with tirzepatide or dulaglutide: SURPASS-CVOT analysis
abstract: AIMS: The impact of tirzepatide and dulaglutide on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and heart failure (HF) outcomes according to HF status is unknown. METHODS AND RESULTS: Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were treated with tirzepatide up to 15 mg or dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly (average 4 years). The incidence of MACE-3 [cardiovascular (CV) death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke], MACE-4 (CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization) and composite of all-cause or CV death and hospitalization or urgent visits for HF were analysed in patients with and without a history of HF. A history of HF (20.3%) was associated with more coronary artery disease and prior MI. Incidences of event categories were higher in the HF group. The hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause death or hospitalization or urgent visits for HF on tirzepatide vs. dulaglutide was 0.83 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.70-0.99] in patients with HF and 0.88 (95%CI 0.78-1.00) without HF. The HR for CV death or hospitalization or urgent visits for HF was 0.85 (95%CI 0.70-1.03) and 0.96 (95%CI 0.83-1.12), for MACE-3 0.90 (95%CI 0.76-1.08) and 0.93 (95%CI 0.83-1.04), and for MACE-4 0.81 (95%CI 0.69-0.95) and 0.91 (95%CI 0.83-1.00) in patients with and without HF, respectively. The patient-reported outcomes of APPADL and EQ-5D-5L visual analogue scores improved and were higher on tirzepatide in both groups. CONCLUSION: With overall non-inferiority established, this exploratory analysis revealed lower rates of the composite of all-cause death or HF events, or MACE-4 among patients with T2D and HF treated with tirzepatide compared with dulaglutide.

title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

title: Cardiovascular Complications of Chronic Liver Disease
abstract: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms-including inflammation, endothelial injury, and neurohormonal overactivation-that contribute to the development of adverse myocardial remodeling, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary vascular syndromes, and cirrhosis-associated cardiovascular syndromes are reviewed. A specific focus is placed on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the most common form of chronic liver disease, while highlighting the distinct cardiovascular manifestations associated with other types of chronic liver disease. These include alcohol-associated liver disease and infiltrative diseases that affect the liver and heart with cardiovascular implications across the spectrum from early stages of liver disease through cirrhosis. We discuss practical approaches to detecting liver disease, including the assessment of liver fibrosis noninvasively in individuals at risk. We discuss the approach to assessing cardiovascular risk through cardiac imaging, biomarkers, and cardiac functional testing once chronic liver disease is detected. Management considerations for commonly encountered cardiovascular conditions and a critical appraisal of the evolving evidence supporting cardiometabolic therapies in patients with chronic liver disease are discussed to underscore potential cardiovascular and liver benefits. Critical evidence gaps and future research priorities are identified, including the development and evaluation of liver-informed cardiovascular risk models, incorporation of cardiovascular end points into liver disease trials, and implementation of integrated cardiohepatometabolic care pathways. Improved recognition of chronic liver disease and related cardiovascular disease risk represents a major opportunity to facilitate earlier disease detection, enhance risk stratification, and improve outcomes across the spectrum of chronic liver disease.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study
abstract: BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR. METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death. RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037). CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and long-term revascularization burden: a recurrent-event analysis of the UK Biobank
abstract: AIMS: To investigate whether elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with cumulative coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization burden in a primary prevention cohort. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 237 729 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry free of ASCVD at baseline, followed for a median of 14.1 years. Lp(a) was analysed using the ESC/EAS 2025 threshold of 105 nmol/L and continuously (per 50 nmol/L increment). The primary outcome was the total number of coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization procedures per person. Given the genetically determined, lifelong nature of Lp(a) exposure, to capture the full sequence of procedures over time, rather than time-to-first-event alone, we applied recurrent-event statistical models, including the Andersen-Gill model, negative binomial regression, and the Prentice-Williams-Peterson gap-time model. Overall, 10 731 revascularization procedures occurred in 237 729 participants. The proportion undergoing ≥1 procedure was higher with Lp(a) ≥ 105 vs. <105 nmol/L (4.36% vs. 2.96%), with larger differences for ≥2 (1.53% vs. 0.95%) and ≥3 procedures (0.36% vs. 0.18%). In Andersen-Gill analysis, Lp(a) ≥ 105 nmol/L was associated with a higher revascularization rate (HR 1.50, 1.42-1.60), with a 55% higher rate of revascularization procedures during follow-up by negative binomial regression (IRR 1.55, 1.45-1.65). The association was strongest for the first procedure (HR 1.48, 1.40-1.56), attenuated for the second (HR 1.28, 1.09-1.50), and non-significant for the third (HR 1.23, 0.94-1.62). Findings were consistent across coronary and peripheral territories. CONCLUSION: In this large primary prevention cohort, elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with a higher long-term revascularization burden across multiple vascular territories. The association was robust for coronary, supportive for peripheral, and inconclusive for carotid revascularization owing to limited statistical power. These findings, derived from recurrent-event methodology, provide a more complete quantification of Lp(a)-associated cardiovascular procedural risk than time-to-first-event analyses alone.

title: The Impact of Statin Therapy on Postoperative Short- and Long-term Mortality and Morbidity After Non-Cardiac Surgery
abstract: AIMS: Statins' anti-inflammatory and endothelial-stabilising effects suggest perioperative value, but trials of de novo initiation were discredited following research misconduct. Whether established preoperative statin therapy lowers postoperative mortality dose-dependently remains unclear. METHODS: We studied 56,362 patients aged ≥45 years undergoing non-cardiac surgery at two university hospitals (2016-2023). Preoperative statin exposure was assessed as status (any vs none), intensity (high vs low/intermediate), and regimen (high vs low/intermediate vs none). Primary outcomes were 30- and 365-day mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting, using random forest-estimated propensity scores targeting the average treatment effect in the treated, was applied to balance measured confounders. Associations were estimated with weighted Cox regression. RESULTS: Overall, 372 patients (0.6%) died within 30 days and 3,735 (6.6%) within 365 days. After weighting, all covariates were balanced. Statin therapy showed a directionally consistent but non-significant association with lower 30-day mortality (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.57-1.07), and was associated with lower 365-day mortality (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.73-0.90; ARD -1.2 percentage points; number needed to treat 83). A dose-response relationship was evident: versus no statin, high-intensity therapy showed a 29% lower hazard (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.60-0.83; ARD -2.3 points) and low/intermediate-intensity a 16% lower hazard (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.74-0.96). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults undergoing non-cardiac surgery, established preoperative statin therapy was associated with dose-dependent lower 365-day mortality. These findings suggest perioperative statin continuation as a preventive strategy and warrant confirmation in a randomised trial.

title: Risk-weighted apoB and lipoprotein-associated coronary risk across ethnic groups
abstract: AIMS: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) reflects the number of circulating atherogenic lipoproteins but does not account for differences in particle atherogenicity. Risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB), which incorporates triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)), may better capture lipoprotein-driven coronary risk, but its performance across diverse populations remains uncertain. We assessed whether the prespecified triglyceride - and Lp(a)-weighted information captured by RW-apoB was associated with coronary events beyond apoB and compared the discrimination of RW-apoB and measured apoB across ethnicities. METHODS: We analyzed 40,132 participants with 4,509 coronary events from ARIC, CARDIA, MESA, the Framingham Offspring Study, and China Kadoorie Biobank. RW-apoB was calculated using a prespecified equation. Mutually adjusted Cox estimates were pooled within ethnic groups using random-effects meta-analysis. Separate single-marker models compared discrimination. Sensitivity analyses included age and sex adjustment, standardized exposures, hard-events, truncated follow-up, and CKB-specific logistic regression. RESULTS: Mean RW-apoB exceeded apoB by approximately 8 mg/dL in African American and Chinese participants, reflecting higher lipoprotein(a) and triglycerides, respectively. RW-apoB was associated with coronary events conditional on apoB in White, African American, Chinese, and Hispanic participants: hazard ratios per 10 mg/dL were 1.11 (95% CI 1.05-1.18), 1.11 (1.08-1.15), 1.08 (1.05-1.11), and 1.10 (1.01-1.21), respectively. C-indices for RW-apoB versus apoB were 0.630 versus 0.617 in White (P<0.001), 0.606 versus 0.595 in African American (P=0.085), 0.567 versus 0.554 in Chinese (P=0.014), and 0.540 versus 0.535 in Hispanic participants (P=0.756). CONCLUSION: RW-apoB captured lipoprotein-associated risk beyond measured apoB, with discrimination gains statistically demonstrable in the larger White and Chinese groups.

title: Association of Non-Cytochrome P450 3A4-Metabolized Statins Versus Atorvastatin With Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Cancer Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Propensity Score-Matched Target Trial Emulation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) often undergo CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4) metabolism. Atorvastatin is a CYP3A4 substrate, whereas rosuvastatin and pitavastatin largely bypass this pathway. We evaluated whether statin choice was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events in TKI-treated patients with cancer. METHODS: Using TriNetX, we conducted an active-comparator, new-user target trial emulation among adults with cancer receiving their first TKI. The index date was the first statin dispensation; outcome ascertainment began on Day 30 and continued up to 3 years. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons included rosuvastatin versus atorvastatin (primary; 2215 per group), pitavastatin comparisons, and a pooled non-CYP3A4 statin comparison. RESULTS: Among 10 843 eligible patients (mean age, 66.7 years; 60.7% male), rosuvastatin was associated with a lower major adverse cardiovascular events rate than atorvastatin (624 versus 769 events; hazard ratio [HR], 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.93]). The proportional-hazards assumption was violated (P=0.042), so the HR was interpreted as a time-averaged association. The pooled comparison was concordant (HR, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.78-0.96]). The early-persistence Day-180 estimate was imprecise (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.73-1.09]). CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin use was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events than atorvastatin in TKI-treated patients with cancer. This observational finding is compatible with, but does not establish, a CYP3A4-mediated interaction. Residual confounding, nonaligned TKI and statin timing in part of the primary cohort, and lack of individual-level event-time data require prospective confirmation.

title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I2 = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I2 = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI. METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207). RESULTS: After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I2 = 0%; τ2 = 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups. CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy
abstract: BACKGROUND: The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE. METHODS: This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO. RESULTS: Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001). Adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently under the OMI/NOMI approach (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001), without reduction in angiographic yield. CONCLUSIONS: An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO. METHODS: The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed. RESULTS: Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P < 0.001), ventricular arrhythmias (4.9% vs 2.0% vs 1.3%; P < 0.001), and in-hospital cardiac arrest (6.1% vs 2.7% vs 1.6%; P < 0.001). Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001). Using a definition of ACO including TIMI flow grade 0 or 1, NSTEMI-ACO accounted for 216,054 presentations (24.4% of NSTEMI). In-hospital outcomes were similarly worse compared with NSTEMI-no-ACO and better compared with STEMI. CONCLUSIONS: ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.

title: Frequency and Prognosis of Alternative Definitions of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Across the Whole Spectrum of Acute Coronary Syndromes
abstract: BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) refers to a myocardial infarction caused by a persistent or transient, complete or near-complete coronary artery occlusion. Multiple definitions have been proposed, yet their frequency and comparative prognostic relevance remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the frequency and prognosis of previously proposed OMI definitions across the whole spectrum of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the MATRIX trial. METHODS: Five alternative OMI definitions were assessed: 1) culprit artery (CA) TIMI flow grade 0; 2) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-1; 3) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2; 4) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >30× upper reference limit; and 5) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or CA-TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >100× upper reference limit. The endpoint of interest was 1-year all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Among 6,558 patients with ACS, OMI frequency ranged from 37.8% for definition 1 to 76.1% for definition 4. OMI was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality according to definitions 1-4 (adjusted HR: 2.08 [95% CI: 1.56-2.78], 1.97[1.47-2.63], 1.70 [1.25-2.32], 1.47 [1.01-2.12], respectively) but not according to definition 5 (adjusted HR: 1.26 [0.90-1.75]). OMI definitions exclusively based on impaired CA flow (ie, definitions 1-3) improved discrimination, reclassification, and model fit when added to the conventional STE/NSTE-ACS classification. One-year mortality did not differ among patients with NSTE-ACS with OMI definition 1 or 2 compared with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) patients. CONCLUSIONS: OMI defined by impaired CA flow confers prognostic implications beyond the presence or absence of ST-segment elevation in a broad ACS population and identifies patients without ST-segment elevation with 1-year mortality similar to that of STEMI.

title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock
abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a heterogeneous syndrome associated with persistently high mortality despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support. One recent randomized controlled trial suggested a mortality benefit of a percutaneous microaxial flow pump in a cohort of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by CS, whereas routine veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in populations with acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS has not improved survival and is associated with higher complication rates. These findings underscore the importance of phenotype-driven patient selection, incorporating the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) and Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) classifications to guide device selection, timing, escalation, and de-escalation. This clinical consensus statement from the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) updates the 2020 expert consensus document and provides updated practical guidance based on the recent evidence on the use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS. Emphasis is placed on patient/device selection according to recent evidence, multidisciplinary shock teams, regionalized hub-and-spoke systems, structured protocols for escalation and futility, and the integration of contemporary trial data and best practices to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.

title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation
abstract: IMPORTANCE: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming. OBJECTIVE: To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system. RESULTS: Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care. OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH). METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization. RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious. CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of NT-proBNP thresholds in Dyspneic Patients in the Emergency Department according to patients' characteristics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Concentrations of N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is central to acute heart failure (AHF) diagnosis in dyspneic emergency departments (ED) patients, but optimal thresholds remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of various NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF, across the general population and these key subgroups. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, including studies published up to August 28, 2025, that reported the diagnostic performance of NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF in dyspneic ED patients. RESULTS: The analysis included 31 studies comprising 26,948 patients. To exclude AHF, a fixed threshold of ≤300 ng/L yielded an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.73 (0.69-0.77), with high sensitivity of 97.9% (96.9-98.5) and lower specificity of 46.2% (36.4-56.2); the negative predictive value of this threshold was 97.0% (96.5-97.4). Age-dependent thresholds (≥450 ng/L for patients aged <50 years, ≥900 ng/L for those aged 50-75 years, and ≥1,800 ng/L for those aged ≥75 years), evaluated in 14,410 patients, achieved an AUC of 0.84 (0.83-0.85) with a more favorable balance between sensitivity of 85.9% (85.0-86.7) and specificity of 82.0% (81.2-82.9). In patients with CKD (N=2,271), all fixed thresholds yielded AUC <0.80; age-dependent thresholds showed an AUC of 0.77 (0.75-0.78) with specificity of 62.6% (59.4-65.7). In patients with obesity (body mass index ≥30), only age-dependent thresholds were assessed, in 3,562 patients; AUC was 0.82 (0.81-0.84) and sensitivity was 81.2% (79.2-83.1), broadly comparable to the overall population. CONCLUSION: A threshold ≤300 ng/L provides excellent rule-out performance for AHF, while age-dependent NT-proBNP thresholds offer superior diagnostic performance for ruling in AHF in the ED compared to fixed thresholds, and demonstrate consistent accuracy across subgroups. However, evidence in patients with CKD and obesity remains limited, both in terms of sample size and the range of thresholds evaluated.

title: Long-Term Safety and Procedural Performance of an Interatrial Shunt for Heart Failure According to Ejection Fraction
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term device durability and phenotype-specific safety outcomes after interatrial shunting require further characterization. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the procedural success, device durability, and heart failure (HF) phenotype-specific safety outcomes of an interatrial shunt in the RELIEVE-HF trial. METHODS: Randomized patients were assigned 1:1 to shunt or sham control with prespecified stratification by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) into heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (LVEF ≤40%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (LVEF >40%). Procedural performance, device durability, serious adverse events (SAEs), major adverse cardiovascular or neurological events (MACNE), major bleeding, and renal outcomes were assessed through 2 years. RESULTS: Among 605 enrolled patients (508 randomized; 97 roll-in), shunt implantation was attempted in 370 and was successful in 369 (99.7%). Among implanted patients with follow-up (n = 348), no device- or procedure-related MACNE occurred through 2 years (0%; 95% CI: 0%-0.9%), and shunt patency was 99.4% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.9%). Prespecified LVEF-stratified analyses demonstrated divergent safety profiles. In HFrEF, shunt therapy was not associated with excess all-cause MACNE, major bleeding, or renal decline and was associated with lower SAE burden. In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline. CONCLUSIONS: Interatrial shunt implantation was mechanically reliable and durable through 2 years. Safety outcomes differed by HF phenotype, with no evidence of excess clinical safety events in HFrEF but increased adverse events in HFpEF. These findings support phenotype-specific evaluation of interatrial shunt therapy. (REducing Lung congestion symptoms using the v-wavE shunt in adVancEd Heart Failure [RELIEVE-HF]; NCT03499236).

title: Genotype and arrhythmic risk in dilated cardiomyopathy
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) presents with variable risk of life-threatening arrhythmias. Genetic diagnosis guides sudden death prevention strategies, but risk magnitude for arrhythmogenic genes remains unknown. This study leveraged the international Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe) to address this gap and improve risk stratification. METHODS: Effects of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in genes associated with DCM and ventricular arrhythmia on clinical events were analysed in DCM-SHaRe patients. Patients were stratified by presence of a P/LP variant in a high-arrhythmogenic risk gene (LMNA, DSP, FLNC, RBM20, PLN, SCN5A, DES, TMEM43), a low-arrhythmogenic risk gene (TTN, TNNT2, MYH7, others), or gene-elusive. Outcomes included age-, sex-, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-adjusted risk of major ventricular arrhythmia (MVA), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), death, and their composite. RESULTS: Among 2660 genotyped adults with DCM (mean diagnosis age 47 ± 15 years, 39.8% female), 434 (16%) had P/LP variants in high-arrhythmogenic genes, 451 (17%) in low-arrhythmogenic genes, and 1775 (67%) were gene-elusive. Compared with gene-elusive patients, patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants showed increased MVA [hazard ratio (HR) 3.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.63-4.01], AF (HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.96-2.98), HF (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.89-3.19), and composite (HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.69-2.29) risk, which remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, and LVEF. Patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants and LVEF ≥ 50% maintained increased MVA (HR 2.36, 95% CI 1.59-3.51) and composite (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.25-2.12) risk. CONCLUSIONS: Genetic testing enables powerful risk stratification for arrhythmias and HF in DCM independent of age, sex, or LVEF.

title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. METHODS: In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0-42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P<0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm2, regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm2, regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%-13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07-1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05-1.38]). CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

title: Early Introduction and Prolonged Full-Dose Anakinra Reduce Recurrence Risk After Discontinuation in Recurrent Pericarditis: An International Multicenter Cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anakinra is effective in recurrent pericarditis, yet optimal treatment duration and strategies for safe drug discontinuation remain uncertain. Identifying predictors of sustained remission after discontinuation is important for clinical management. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 185 consecutive adult patients with corticosteroid-dependent and colchicine-resistant refractory recurrent pericarditis across 16 international referral centers, who permanently discontinued therapy after clinical remission. The primary end point was pericarditis recurrence after drug discontinuation. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to identify demographic, clinical, and therapeutic predictors of postdiscontinuation relapse. RESULTS: Among 185 patients who discontinued anakinra (58.4% women, mean age 50.4±17.8 years, 77% idiopathic cause), treatment was initiated a median of 10 months (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-19.5) after the first episode and continued at 100 mg/d for a median of 6 months (IQR, 4-12). Over a median follow-up of 7.2 months (IQR, 1.5-23.3) after discontinuation, 68 patients (36.8%) experienced recurrence, with a median time to recurrence of 2.1 months (IQR, 0.7-8.5). Initiation within 12 months from the first pericarditis episode and maintenance of full-dose therapy (100 mg/d) for ≥6 months were independently associated with lower recurrence risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.33 [95% CI, 0.18-0.66]; P=0.001 and HR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-0.86]; P=0.017; respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Early initiation of anakinra and maintenance of full-dose therapy for at least 6 months are associated with a significantly lower risk of relapse after discontinuation and may inform treatment duration and discontinuation strategies in recurrent pericarditis.

title: Machine Learning of Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Myocardial Radiomics for Identification of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is an important cause of heart failure (HF) with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness that can be challenging to distinguish from other LV hypertrophic processes. Echocardiographic myocardial radiomic texture analysis may identify imperceptible amyloid-induced structural changes. OBJECTIVES: The study aims to develop and validate an echocardiography-based machine learning model using myocardial radiomics to identify ATTR-CM. METHODS: In this retrospective and prospective multicenter study, 854 echocardiographic scans were analyzed. Conventional and novel radiomic features were extracted from parasternal short-axis views at basal, mid, and apical LV levels, with incorporated age and sex from echocardiogram metadata. A machine learning pipeline was developed using a balanced training set (150 ATTR-CM, 150 nonamyloid HF). Performance was evaluated on an independent internal validation set (50 ATTR-CM, 399 nonamyloid HF) and an external validation set (10 ATTR-CM, 10 immunoglobulin light-chain-amyloid, 10 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, 75 nonamyloid HF). RESULTS: In internal validation, the model achieved 86% sensitivity (95% CI: 73.8%-93%), 92% specificity (95% CI: 88.9%-94.3%), 57.3% positive predictive value (95% CI: 46.1%-67.9%), 98.1% negative predictive value (NPV) (95% CI: 96.2%-99.1%), and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve 0.938 (95% CI: 0.891-0.985). Performance was consistent in the external validation (100% sensitivity, 78.9% specificity, 33.3% positive predictive value, 100% NPV, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve of 0.917). The model correctly classified 77.3% of nonamyloid HF, 70% of AL-amyloid cases, and 100% of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy cases as non-ATTR in subgroup analysis. CONCLUSIONS: We developed an echocardiographic radiomics-based tool to identify ATTR-CM with excellent discrimination and very high NPV in a cohort that approximates clinical experience. These preliminary findings require validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

title: Cardiovascular effects of continued vs. discontinued anabolic-androgenic steroid use: a longitudinal follow-up study
abstract: AIMS: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is prevalent among men engaged in strength training and is associated with adverse structural and functional cardiac changes, but longitudinal data are lacking. This follow-up study examined myocardial effects of AAS with continued use and reversibility following discontinuation. METHODS AND RESULTS: Participants of a previously published cohort (2017-19) of 101 AAS users and 71 non-using weightlifting controls (WLCs) were invited for a follow-up study and underwent interviews, hormonal profiling, and transthoracic echocardiography. Current AAS users at baseline were continued or discontinued users at follow-up, while former users at baseline were those with continued abstinence and those who relapsed.Among those re-enrolled, 70 were AAS users, of whom 35 continued, 15 discontinued, 14 maintained abstinence, and 6 relapsed, and 35 were WLCs. Continued AAS users had persistent indexed left ventricular mass (LVMI 119 ± 30 g/m2), reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF 48 ± 10%), and worsened diastolic function. Continued AAS users receiving antihypertensive therapy showed improved LVEF compared with untreated users (Δ = 5 ± 8 vs. -4 ± 8%, P = 0.005). Discontinued AAS users showed reduction in LVMI (Δ = -21 g/m2, P = 0.01) and improved LVEF (Δ = 6%, P < 0.001). At follow-up, these changes were comparable with WLCs, which showed statistically but clinically insignificant differences. CONCLUSION: Continued AAS use was associated with sustained LV hypertrophy, LV systolic dysfunction, and worsening diastolic function. Antihypertensive therapy among ongoing AAS users was associated with improved LV systolic function. Discontinuation of AAS use was associated with improvement in cardiac structure and function towards values observed in WLCs.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation
abstract: AIMS: The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR. METHODS AND RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE. CONCLUSIONS: In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

title: Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Class I Obesity: A Propensity-Matched Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity may increase the technical complexity of robotic mitral valve (MV) repair, but comparative outcomes with sternotomy remain poorly defined. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic vs sternotomy MV repair in patients with class I obesity. METHODS: A total of 880 patients with class I obesity (body mass index 30-34.9 kg/m2) underwent MV repair at our clinic between 2008 and 2025. After excluding those with mitral stenosis, active endocarditis, prior sternotomy, or concomitant procedures, 429 patients remained. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 132 patients in each group who underwent either robotic or conventional sternotomy MV repair. RESULTS: Median age was 59 years (IQR: 52-66), and 81% were male. Cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were longer in the robotic group than in the sternotomy group (86 vs 65 minutes and 60 vs 48 minutes, respectively; P < 0.001). Robotic MV repair was associated with shorter hospitalization (3.5 vs 5 days; P < 0.001) and a lower postoperative transfusion rate (1.5% vs 10.6%; P = 0.002). There were no operative deaths in either group. No sternal wound infections occurred. Thirty-day readmission was numerically higher after robotic repair (12.8% vs 4.3%; P = 0.064). Ten-year survival was 92% (95% CI: 87% to 97%) with no significant difference between groups (P = 0.83). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with class I obesity, the robotic approach in comparison to sternotomy was associated with lower transfusion rates, shorter hospitalization, and comparable operative mortality and long-term survival relative to sternotomy. Although 30-day readmission was numerically higher among robotic patients, most events were minor and managed without intervention.

title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations
abstract: BACKGROUND: The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment. METHODS: In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method. RESULTS: The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSIONS: Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

title: Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes
abstract: Right ventricular (RV) size and function inform prognosis in many cardiovascular diseases, but assessment by two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography is challenging. Here we show that a deep learning model, Dimensional Reconstruction of Imaging Data-Right Ventricle (DROID-RV), can estimate RV end-diastolic diameter and identify RV systolic dysfunction from transthoracic echocardiography videos. We trained DROID-RV in 17,141 ambulatory cardiology patients (51,188 studies and 383,881 video clips) and validated model predictions in 9,112 primary care patients and 831 patients with RV ejection fraction assessed by three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. Across multiple test samples, DROID-RV accurately estimates RV end-diastolic diameter and identifies RV dysfunction, although model prediction error increases at extremes of RV size and function. We additionally show that RV size and function predictions are associated with incident mortality, atrial fibrillation and heart failure. Our work demonstrates how deep learning can automate RV assessment and risk stratification at scale using two-dimensional echocardiography.

title: Left Ventricular Filling Pressure Classification by Electrocardiogram, Echocardiography, and Catheterization: Prognostic Implications
abstract: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular diastolic filling pressure (LVFP) is a hallmark of heart failure. Although pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) measured during right heart catheterization (RHC) is the reference standard, echocardiography is more commonly used in practice. OBJECTIVES: The authors previously developed an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) algorithm, trained on echocardiographic assessment, to classify LVFP. The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic implications of LVFP classification by AI-ECG, echocardiography, and PAWP among patients undergoing temporally proximate testing. METHODS: Adults who underwent echocardiography with electrocardiography within 14 days and RHC within 30 days were included. Elevated LVFP was defined as PAWP ≥15 mm Hg, grade 2 or 3 diastolic dysfunction by echocardiography, or elevated LVFP as classified by AI-ECG. Associations with all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed. RESULTS: Among 4,168 patients (median age: 64 years; 47.7% women), elevated LVFP was classified by AI-ECG in 2,383 patients, by echocardiography in 1,643, and by PAWP in 1,841. AI-ECG showed good discrimination for echocardiographic LVFP (AUC: 0.879; 95% CI: 0.867-0.891) and moderate discrimination for PAWP (AUC: 0.711; 95% CI: 0.695-0.727). Over 7.7 years, 1,433 deaths occurred. Elevated LVFP classification by AI-ECG (adjusted HR [aHR]: 1.80; 95% CI: 1.55-2.09) and echocardiography (aHR: 1.74; 95% CI: 1.51-2.02) showed stronger associations with mortality than PAWP (aHR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.31); in discordant cases, AI-ECG better predicted survival. Similar associations were observed for major adverse cardiovascular events. CONCLUSIONS: Despite moderate agreement with PAWP, echocardiography and AI-ECG showed stronger associations with clinical outcomes, suggesting they capture prognostically relevant myocardial information beyond resting hemodynamic status.

title: A multiview video-text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography
abstract: Invasive coronary angiography is the reference standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, yet assessment is subjective, and existing artificial-intelligence tools typically assess stenosis in individual frames or videos and do not integrate the full multiview angiographic study. Here we show that DeepCORO-CLIP, trained on 203,808 angiographic videos and reports from 28,117 patients, interprets whole multiple-video angiograms at once. It detects obstructive stenoses (≥70%), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.89 internally and externally, and identifies chronic total occlusion (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.95), intra-coronary thrombus and calcification (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.91). It also predicts 1-year cardiovascular events (AUROC = 0.79, 95% CI of 0.74 to 0.84, versus 0.65 for a model derived using clinical variables) and left ventricular ejection fraction (mean absolute error 7.3% versus 8.8% for a previous model), both achieved using coronary angiography alone. In a blinded review of 365 evaluations across 288 angiograms, its reports were clinically usable in 76% of evaluations versus 88% for cardiologists, with comparable false positives (17% versus 14%, P = 0.38); residual missed stenoses reflected an adjustable threshold rather than an absent signal.

title: Algorithmic Guardrails for Echocardiography AI: Deep Feature Representations for Error Slicing and Selective LVEF Estimation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Automated echocardiography analysis using artificial intelligence (AI) currently lacks effective guardrails or oversight mechanisms to ensure its safe and reliable deployment. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated whether deep feature representations can identify echocardiograms at risk of misinterpretation by echocardiography AI-based left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) estimation models. METHODS: We retrospectively validated 2 state-of-the-art models for LVEF estimation, EchoNet (single-task model) and PanEcho (multitask foundation model), on 4,010 apical-4-chamber videos from 1,353 studies (n = 1,208) with biplane LVEF measurements in the MIMIC-IV-ECHO database (2017-2019). We extracted 4 deep feature representations from a view classifier, a left ventricle segmentation model, and the 2 validated LVEF estimation models. These features were evaluated for their ability to identify systematic misinterpretations (error slicing) and automatically exclude AI estimates for high-risk inputs (selective estimation). RESULTS: While PanEcho performed better relative to EchoNet (EchoNet minus PanEcho [Δ], Δmean absolute error: 0.31 [0.07, 0.55]; ΔR2: -0.07 [-0.11, -0.03]), both models systematically overestimated LVEF at lower values (proportional bias slope, EchoNet: -0.33 [-0.39, -0.28], P < 0.001, PanEcho: -0.31 [-0.36, -0.26], P < 0.001). All investigated deep feature representations identified error slices for both models. Shared error slices between the models revealed 2 common failure modes: contrast-enhanced echocardiograms and poor-quality apical-4-chamber views. Selective estimation using intermediate features from EchoNet achieved the best performance across both estimation models (area under risk-coverage curve, EchoNet: 5.04 [4.45, 5.66]; PanEcho: 5.21 [4.54, 5.92]). CONCLUSIONS: Deep feature representations can be leveraged to identify and automatically flag misinterpretation-prone echocardiograms, enabling promising guardrail mechanisms for the reliable deployment of echocardiography AI.

title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, yet recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) challenged these findings. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings. METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses.
