The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses. RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62). CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR. METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed. RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).

title: Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention
abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.

title: Clinical Impact of Physiology-Guided PCI: 1-year Results of the Post-Revascularization Optimization and Physiological Evaluation of Intermediate Lesions using Fractional Flow Reserve (PROPHET-FFR) Study
abstract: Background: The clinical value of physiological assessment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We evaluated clinical outcomes associated with post-PCI physiology and temporal trends in its adoption. Methods: PROPHET-FFR (NCT05056662) is an ambispective observational study of patients undergoing invasive physiological assessment of intermediate coronary stenoses. Patients were categorized into three strategies: deferred revascularization based on non-ischemic physiology (deferred PCI), PCI for ischemic lesions without post-PCI physiological assessment (conventional PCI), and physiology-guided PCI with post-PCI assessment and optimization when indicated (post-PCI physiology). Temporal trends in the use of post-PCI physiology and physiology-guided optimization were evaluated, together with the incidence of 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Propensity score matching between conventional PCI and post-PCI physiology was performed to confirm the primary findings. Results: Among 1,986 patients, 1,307 underwent deferred PCI, 331 conventional PCI, and 348 post-PCI physiology. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 4.1%, 7.6%, and 3.4%, respectively (p=0.011). Compared with conventional-PCI, post-PCI physiology had lower MACE (3.4% vs 7.6%; p=0.019), primarily driven by reduced TVR (2.6% vs 5.4%; p=0.057), with consistent findings after propensity score matching (226 patients/group; 2.7% vs 8.0%; p=0.0114). Post-PCI physiology increased from 11.8% to 22.8% across registry phases (p<0.001), with a numerical increase in physiology-guided optimization (11.6% vs 18.1%; p=0.08). Conclusions: In this observational study, post-PCI physiology appears to be associated with lower 12-month MACE compared with conventional PCI, with consistent findings after propensity score matching.

title: Trends in Use of Coronary Angiography, Percutaneous Coronary Intervention, and Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Over a Decade in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass graft are among the most commonly performed procedures globally. The influence of recent scientific evidence on national-level temporal trends remains poorly explored. METHODS: The frequency, characteristics, and outcomes of elective and nonelective coronary angiography, PCI, and coronary artery bypass graft were described using the French National Hospitalization Database from 2014 to 2023 (covering a population of 67.0 million inhabitants), totaling 6 290 951 coronary interventions among 2 985 822 patients (mean age, 67.8±12.2 years; 69.9% men). RESULTS: Over 10 years, the annual number of coronary interventions increased by 33%, driven by a rise in coronary angiography (+32%) and PCI (+40%), while coronary artery bypass graft decreased (-8%). The growth in PCI was predominantly related to an increase in elective procedures (from 53.5% to 56.9%, P<0.001), particularly among older patients (+73%), and in multivessel disease (from 16.7% in 2014-2015 to 19.0% in 2022-2023, P<0.001). Attempts to recanalize chronic total coronary occlusion doubled (from 1.9% to 3.3%, P<0.001). In-hospital death after PCI decreased (from 2.05% in 2014 to 1.58% in 2023, P for trend<0.001), with the most notable improvements observed in nonelective PCI. Similarly, in-hospital death after coronary artery bypass graft declined (from 3.5% to 2.9%, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore a significant increase in both coronary angiography and PCI over the past decade in France, particularly in procedures classified as elective among older patients. This trend raises questions about the influence of recent scientific evidence and guidelines on clinical practice in this country.

title: Physical activity, atrial fibrillation and the dose-response relationship: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Regular physical activity (PA) may reduce atrial fibrillation (AF) risk in the general population, however, contemporary data suggests individuals engaging in the highest levels of PA may exhibit a paradoxical rise in AF risk. The point at which the dose-response curve reverses remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the association between PA and AF across the full continuum of PA exposure. METHODS: Four databases were searched (from January 1990 to June 2025). Eligible studies included those that reported PA exposure compared against a sedentary control group and assessed AF incidence or prevalence. PA exposures were standardised to metabolic equivalent of task hours per week (MET-hr/wk). Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using a weighted random-effects model. A weighted restricted cubic spline model of logarithmic odds was used to produce a dose-response curve. RESULTS: 37 studies were included (n = 1,298,291 individuals). In the general population, PA was associated with a reduction in odds of AF by 22% (22 studies; OR 0.78; 95% CI 0.68, 0.89). Athlete status was associated with an increase in the odds of AF (15 studies; OR 2.74; 95% CI 1.72, 4.39). Dose-response analysis (26 studies; n = 1,022,790 individuals) showed 26 MET-hr/wk of PA was associated with the greatest reduction in odds of AF, with doses beyond 78 MET-hr/wk associated with increased odds of AF; the equivalent of 6-7 hours per week of endurance training. CONCLUSION: PA and AF demonstrate a U-shaped relationship whereby beyond a quantitative dose threshold of 78 MET-hr/wk, the protective effect of exercise may reverse.

title: Stroke Risk-Based Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: ALONE-AF Post-Hoc Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Discontinuation of oral anticoagulant (OAC) in patients without recurrent atrial arrhythmia after ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) has been demonstrated to reduce composite outcomes of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding compared with continued OAC. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the optimal OAC strategy according to baseline stroke risk and AF recurrence. METHODS: In this post-hoc analysis of the Long-Term Anticoagulation Discontinuation after Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF) trial, patients were stratified according to CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 and ≥3. Within each stratum, outcomes were compared between the OAC discontinuation and continuation subgroups. The cumulative incidence of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding at 2 years was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with competing risk analysis accounting for AF recurrence. RESULTS: Among 840 patients, 584 and 256 had a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 (mean age 62.0±7.5 years, 15.9% female) and ≥3 (mean age 68.9±7.3 years, 45.3% female), respectively. In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≤2 stratum, the primary outcome occurred in one patient (0.4%) in discontinuation subgroup vs. six (2.4%) in continuation subgroup (absolute difference -1.9 percentage points, P=0.066). In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3 stratum, two events (1.8%) occurred in the continuation subgroup only (absolute difference -1.8 percentage points, P=0.172). All major bleeding events (n=5) occurred in the continuation subgroups. Competing risk analysis yielded consistent results. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, no statistically significant differences in outcomes were observed between OAC strategies when stratified by CHA2DS2-VASc score, though event numbers were limited. Larger prospective trials are needed to confirm these observations. TRIAL REGISTRATIONS: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04432220.

title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR. METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months. RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

title: Evolution of Tined Leadless Pacemaker Implantation: Patient Selection, Implant Volume, Center Characteristics, and Safety Trends
abstract: BACKGROUND: As leadless pacing approaches a decade in clinical practice, we sought to assess how device complications have changed over time, and how variations in patient, implanter volume, and facility characteristics are associated with these changes. OBJECTIVE: To examine rates of cardiac perforations after leadless pacemaker implantation over time, and the associations between patient, implanter volume, and facility characteristics with these outcomes, including the extent of variation attributable to implanters and facilities. METHODS: Medicare claims linked to a manufacturer's device registration data were used to identify patients implanted with a tined leadless pacemaker from 2017 to 2024. Patient selection across implanters and facilities was evaluated by examining differences in patient characteristics and their impact on patient-adjusted model estimates. Random-intercept models were fitted to estimate variation attributable to implanters and facilities. RESULTS: Among 46,698 implants, 19,446 (41.6%) were Micra AV; patients had a mean age of 80.4 years and a high Charlson Comorbidity Index (4.7±3.4). Cardiac perforation rates declined over time (adjusted Coefficient -0.13, 95% CI -0.19 - -0.06, p-value<0.01). Higher implanter volume was associated with fewer perforations (OR 0.93 per additional 10 implants, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p-value<0.01). Differences in patient characteristics across providers and facilities were observed; however, adjustment for these differences did not materially alter the associations between implanters and facility and perforation rates. CONCLUSION: In Medicare patients with tined leadless pacemakers, cardiac perforation rates declined over time and were lower in those implanted by more experienced implanters. Variation in outcomes was more closely associated with implanters than facilities.

title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications. OBJECTIVE: We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes. METHODS: A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events. RESULTS: We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157). CONCLUSIONS: Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.
